dedupe_keys.name: mapping mining areas in the tropics from 2016 to 2024

description: This panel dataset maps mining areas along the tropical belt for each year from 2016 to 2024. It was produced by Philipp Sepin, Lukas Vashold and Nikolas Kuschnig to analyse the local environmental, social and economic impacts of mining where conventional data are scarce, and accompanies a journal article (doi:10.1038/s41893-025-01668-9) and a working paper. A machine-learning segmentation model, trained on more than 25,000 mining polygons from the literature, delineates mining areas in high-resolution satellite imagery of under 5 m; the result is over 145,000 polygons covering on average 65,000 square kilometres a year, with a reported accuracy of 87.7 percent and precision of 84.1 percent. Licence (read on the provider page on 2026-09-28): ODbL-1.0. Access is free of charge. Caveats: coverage is the tropics only, and the polygons are model predictions with classification errors. For simulation it provides yearly footprints of mining expansion for hazard exposure, land-use change and environmental impact analyses of mining regions. Related catalogue records include the global mining polygons of Maus et al.
